gloss: to negotiate; to call to each other

definitions.explanation: To discuss terms or make a request to someone with authority; to go back and forth in discussion.

definitions.gloss: to call to each other; to exchange words
definitions.explanation: For two or more people to speak to each other, often taking turns in dialogue.

examples.japanese: {値段|ねだん}を{掛|か}け{合|あ}う。
{上司|じょうし}に{掛|か}け{合|あ}って{休暇|きゅうか}をもらった。
examples.english: I negotiated with my boss and got vacation time.

examples.japanese: {市役所|しやくしょ}に{掛|か}け{合|あ}って、{許可|きょか}をもらうことにした。
examples.english: I decided to negotiate with city hall to get permission.
To call out to each other.

examples.japanese: {役者|やくしゃ}たちが{台詞|せりふ}を{掛|か}け{合|あ}う。
{試合中|しあいちゅう}、{選手|せんしゅ}たちは{互|たが}いに{声|こえ}を{掛|か}け{合|あ}っていた。
examples.english: During the game, the players were calling out to each other.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB:
{掛|か}ける (to engage) + {合|あ}う (to do together, mutually)

TRANSITIVITY:
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive) - uses に for the person negotiated with

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- 〜に{掛|か}け{合|あ}う: to negotiate with someone
- {掛|か}け{合|あ}い{漫才|まんざい}: comic dialogue (manzai)
- {台詞|せりふ}を{掛|か}け{合|あ}う: to exchange lines (theater)

RELATED NOUN:
- {掛|か}け{合|あ}い: negotiation; dialogue
